review_note: three lenses (privacy and publication rule, hash rule and tiers, counts and text) each followed by a skeptic per finding; confirmed findings were applied before the RESULT was posted; agent scratch not included

findings.claim: The hash-receipt size check is skipped silently when the size column is not all digits (`if sz.isdigit() and int(sz)!=byp[p]['size']`), so a hash row with a blank or malformed size would be accepted without the size-equality guarantee the README states ('ties each content_hash to the listing by path and byte count').
findings.evidence: Published own/classify_root.py contains the guarded comparison; my independent re-read of all 33 hash part files found 808 rows, 0 non-digit sizes, 0 size mismatches, 0 paths outside the inventory, 0 duplicates, 0 conflicts, so the weakness is latent in this build (receipt accepted=808 matches my count exactly).
findings.fix: Treat a non-digit size as a rejection category (e.g. 'size_missing') instead of falling through to accept; re-run would produce an identical receipt for this build.

findings.claim: The DRIVE_MIRROR_BRANCH label is decided over the truncated `git_paths[:4]` list rather than over every path of the matching blobs, so a blob with more than four recorded paths whose non-drive/ paths sort after the cut would be mislabelled DRIVE_MIRROR_BRANCH instead of BRANCH_OR_HISTORY.
findings.evidence: own/classify_root.py sets f['git_paths']=sorted(...)[:4] and then tests all(... startswith('drive/') for p in f['git_paths']). Recomputing the label from the full path sets in git_index.json for all 89 GIT_EXACT rows gives 0 mismatches (TIP 17, DRIVE_MIRROR_BRANCH 68, BRANCH_OR_HISTORY 4), and every GIT_EXACT hash has exactly one git path, so the truncation is not triggered in this build.
findings.fix: Compute the drive/ test over the untruncated path set (e.g. all(p.startswith('drive/') for e in ents for p in e['paths'])) and truncate only for the stored locator.

findings.claim: The published script de-anonymizes every generic folder label: its LABEL dict maps the real Dropbox folder names (including the 23-, 25- and 31-character ones for the folder C, peer-review packet and the two 'other root folder' labels, and the app-bundle folder) to the labels used in README/aggregate/crosswalk, and the guard's own folder-name tuple repeats four of them. This contradicts 'folders appear only as generic labels' for the whole directory.
findings.evidence: grep -n '^LABEL=' and grep -n 'for seg in' on own/build_root_pub.py show 5 of the 6 real folder names (all except the 4-char one, which is itself the label); cut -f5 inventory_root.tsv | sort -u confirms they are the inventory folder names. The guard only scans files starting with ROOT_/LEDGER_/SUMMARY/README/PINS for folder names, so own/ was never checked (my scan in review_scratch/check_all.py, section B3, reports 6 real-folder hits in own/build_root_pub.py and 3 in own/build_inventory.py).
findings.fix: Do not publish own/build_root_pub.py and own/build_inventory.py as-is: move the LABEL dict and the guard's folder-name tuple into a local, unpublished config (like shared_ns.txt), substitute placeholders on export, and extend the guard's folder-name and inventory-name checks to every file under own/.

findings.claim: The published PERSONAL regex contains a capitalised personal first name used as a personal-item marker (an owner detail), and the folder test on the same script names the two short real root folder names with a comment describing them as the owner's other material.
findings.evidence: review_scratch/c1_quant.py: the regex has exactly one [A-Z][a-z]+ alternation; it matches 3 inventory paths (2 in folder E, 1 in account root), all flagged personal, so it is a real person's name tied to the owner's files. grep -n "r\['folder'\] in (" own/build_inventory.py shows the two real folder names.
findings.fix: Strip the name alternation from the published copy (or load the personal-marker list from a local file) and replace the two folder names with the labels or a placeholder; re-run the guard over own/.

findings.claim: The matched_tokens column publishes fragments of Dropbox file names: each token is a word found in the Dropbox basename stem of the file identified by content_hash, and for most rows that word is not derivable from the public Git path of the located blob.
findings.evidence: review_scratch/c1_quant.py over the 159 rows: 75 token occurrences are in the Dropbox stem but in no Git path basename of the blob; 28 occurrences (all folder B, DRIVE_MIRROR_BRANCH blobs) appear nowhere in any Git path, so the Dropbox name differs from the Drive-mirror name and the token is new information. 18 distinct hashes are affected; for hashes eff9e02e, 015f7ae1 and 13e71a2d the union of tokens reveals 5 of 11, 5 of 12 and 5 of 15 name tokens. The ledger_rows column of ROOT_CROSSWALK.tsv and the per-unit hit counts in LEDGER_ROOT.tsv imply the same association more weakly.
findings.fix: Drop the matched_tokens column (keep match class only), or print it only when the token also occurs in the basename of a public Git path for that blob; state in README that ledger joins on Dropbox names are name evidence that is kept local.

findings.claim: The 'months present (sample)' column (also SUMMARY.json by_folder.months) publishes modification months that pin single files, and for the four single-month folders it gives the modification month of every per-file crosswalk row, contradicting 'No Dropbox path, name or time' for those rows; the '(sample)' label is also inaccurate since every folder's list is complete.
findings.evidence: review_scratch/check_all.py section D: the sampling step is 1 for all 8 folders (all have <=6 months), so the lists are complete. Seven listed (folder, month) pairs correspond to 1-2 files: account root 2023-07 (1), 2024-09 (1), 2026-01 (2), 2026-09 (1); folder A 2026-05 (1); folder D 2025-09 (1); folder E 2025-12 (1). Shared namespace root, folder B, folder C and the folder F list one month each, so 70 of the 99 ROOT_CROSSWALK.tsv rows (32 + 21 + 17) have an inferable modification month.
findings.fix: Replace the column with a coarse range at year granularity, or list a month only when it covers 3+ files and suppress months entirely for folders that have per-file rows; remove '(sample)' or make the sampling real.

findings.claim: The guard's PAT list embeds the leading four digits of both Dropbox namespace ids (the shared namespace and the account namespace) as literal regex prefixes followed by \d{6,}, a partial namespace-id disclosure in a published file.
findings.evidence: python3 -I one-liner: read the two 4-digit literals from the PAT list in own/build_root_pub.py and the distinct ns prefixes from column 1 of inventory_root.tsv; both ns ids (11 digits each) start with one of the two literals (shared namespace matches the first, the other namespace the second). Also confirmed with shared_ns.txt.
findings.fix: Replace the two literal prefixes with a generic 10-12 digit pattern (e.g. (?<!\d)\d{10,12}(?!\d)) or load the prefixes from the local shared_ns.txt at run time.

result.reason: Not refuted; the defect reproduces and the evidence matches exactly. (1) Diffed the published classify script against the local source: identical except the scratch-root placeholder, and it contains the guarded comparison as quoted. (2) Wrote an independent checker (python3 -I) over all 33 hash part files against the inventory: 808 lines, all exactly 3 columns, 0 malformed hashes, 0 non-digit sizes, 0 size mismatches, 0 paths outside the inventory, 0 duplicate paths, 0 conflicts, 808 accepted; every hashable inventory row has a hash and no non-hashable row does, so receipt accepted=808 and rejected={} are correct for this build. (3) Replayed the script's exact accept/reject block on synthetic rows: a digit-string mismatch is rejected as size_mismatch, but blank, alphabetic, negative, space-padded and float-like size strings are all accepted with no rejection category, confirming the silent fall-through. (4) Nothing downstream would catch it: the inventory builder only consumes listing rows whose third column is the literal object type, so hash rows are ignored, and the publication script takes the classified rows and receipt as given. (5) The upstream shape is realistic, not hypothetical: the pipeline's own page parser emits an empty size when metadata lacks one and the inventory builder coerces non-digit sizes to zero, so an empty size string could reach a hash row. The README's claim that the receipt ties each hash to the listing by path and byte count therefore holds for this build only because all 808 rows carried matching digit sizes; the code does not enforce it structurally. Severity LOW is appropriate: no published number, tier or row would change, and the fix would yield an identical receipt; it is a latent robustness gap in published code that the README's guarantee leans on, so NONE would understate it and anything above LOW would overstate it.

Code reading: the published classify script (identical to the local copy except the scratch root placeholder) does build git_paths as sorted(...)[:4] on line 39 and run the all(startswith('drive/')) test over that truncated list on line 40, so the line-level description is accurate. The defect it predicts, however, is unreachable with these inputs, not merely untriggered. I loaded the Git index (32,221 entries) with python3 -I: every entry carries exactly one recorded path (paths-per-blob distribution is {1: 32221}), every key is repo:blob, and a content hash maps to at most 2 entries (324 hashes with 2, all of them the same blob id present in both repos; 31,573 with 1). Because a blob id is content-determined and there are two repos, the union repo:path set per content hash is bounded at 2, so the [:4] cut can never drop a path for any hash in this index; a 'blob with more than four recorded paths' cannot exist in this index format. I recomputed the location label over the full, untruncated path sets for all 89 GIT_EXACT rows in the local rows file: TIP 17, DRIVE_MIRROR_BRANCH 68, BRANCH_OR_HISTORY 4, 0 mismatches against the stored label, stored git_paths equal to the full set in every row (all 89 have exactly one path and one blob), and 0 mismatches against the git_where column of the published crosswalk table; README and SUMMARY counts agree. No published document states a rule for DRIVE_MIRROR_BRANCH in terms of 'every path under drive/'; README and SUMMARY only report the three counts, so no stated rule is contradicted. Also note the truncation can only err in one direction (drive/ paths sorting ahead of a dropped non-drive path) and even that needs 5 or more paths per hash, which the two-repo, one-path-per-blob design excludes. Net: no published number or label is affected and none can be with these inputs; the suggested one-token hardening is harmless but optional. Severity for this build is NONE (a code-hygiene note for reuse of the script against a richer index, at most).
